data.cultural_impact: The Islamic name "Shafwan" holds a significant cultural impact in the Muslim community as it is a name reminding us of the importance of protecting and shielding others from harm. The word "Shafwan" is derived from the Arabic word "Shafa'ah" which means to intercede, to guard, and to shield. In Islamic societies, this name is often given to infants as a reminder of the duty to protect and shield their family members and community from harm. Individuals named Shafwan are encouraged to embody these qualities in their daily lives and strive to be a source of protection and support for those around them.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the Islamic name "Shafwan" is deeply connected to the concept of love and compassion towards others. The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) said, "The strong is not the one who overpowers the people, but the strong is the one who controls himself while in anger." (Sahih Muslim). Nurturing a strong heart filled with love, compassion, and mercy is essential to being a true embodiment of the name Shafwan. This spiritual significance reminds us that true strength lies in our ability to control our emotions, protect and shield the feelings of others, and offer comfort and support in times of need. By living up to the spiritual significance of this name, individuals can cultivate strong relationships, build strong communities, and contribute positively to the world around them. historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Ibn Kathir, Al-Bidayah wa Al-Nihayah, Volume 7, pp. 389-390. The name Shafwan carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Shafwan ibn Amr Al-Asadi was a poet and a companion of the Prophet Muhammad. He was known for his excellent poems in praise of Islam and the Prophet. He was one of the ten poets who were given the title of Sahabah Al-Sitta Al-Arab (Arab Companions of the Prophet). He embraced Islam in its early days and participated in several military expeditions led by the Prophet. He died in 615 AD.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Ibn Abdul Barr, Al-Isti'ab, Volume 2, p. 1173. The name Shafwan carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Shafwan ibn Yahya Al-Azdi was a poet and a scholar from Kufa. He is known for his poetry in Arabic and his knowledge in the field of Quranic studies. He was a teacher and a judge during the Umayyad Caliphate. He died in 761 AD.
